name: Pest season length vs average
title: Pest season length: {city} vs average
alt: Chart comparing the frost-free season in {city}, {SS} with the state average. {summary}

research.ask: "frost_free_days" — the average length of the FROST-FREE period in {city} (days between the last spring freeze and the first autumn freeze), as a plain number; and "frost_free_state_avg" — the same figure averaged across the STATE of {state}, as a plain number, so the city can be compared against it
research.source_ask: "frost_free_source" — the source of those growing-season figures (e.g. "NOAA 1991-2020 Climate Normals")

captions: The frost-free season in {city} runs {self_value}, against {benchmark_value} for the {benchmark}. {difference} Every frost-free day is a day insects can breed, so the length of that window sets how many generations a population gets through in a year.

{city}, {SS} gets {self_value} between freezes where the {benchmark} sees {benchmark_value}. {difference} Pest activity starts when the last freeze passes and ends when the first one arrives — that gap is the season.
{difference} At {self_value} frost-free against {benchmark_value} for the {benchmark}, treatment in {city} has to cover more of the calendar than a state average would suggest.
